citations.locator: Marcion and the Marcionite Churches (A. Harnack)
citations.excerpt: he found it necessary to withdraw from the great church and establish in Rome a community of his own. This was about the year 144.
Heretical sect founded in A.D. 144 at Rome by Marcion
Marcion was son of the Bishop of Sinope in Pontus , born c. A.D. 110

facts.value: about 300 years in the West, longer in the East

citations.excerpt: continuing in the West for 300 years, but in the East some centuries longer, especially outside the Byzantine Empire .

facts.value: Rejected the Old Testament, taught that Christ was Son of a good God distinct from the God of the Old Testament, and used a canon of one gospel (a form of Luke) and ten letters of Paul.

citations.excerpt: They rejected the writings of the Old Testament and taught that Christ was not the Son of the God of the Jews , but the Son of the good God, who was different from the God of the Ancient Covenant.

citations.locator: Marcionites, Mutilation of the New Testament
citations.excerpt: he created his own New Testament admitting but one gospel, a mutilation of St. Luke, and an Apostolicon containing ten epistles of St. Paul .

facts.value: An organized church body founded by Marcion that soon had sister churches in the east and west of the empire.

citations.excerpt: The new society increased in the two following decades; and very soon numerous sister-churches were flourishing in the east and west of the empire.

facts.value_before_verify: An organized church body founded by Marcion at Rome that soon had congregations across the Roman Empire.
